processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel blocks were cast via vacuum arc furnace.
Applied to all steels (shared schedule) to promote uniform composition and microstructure.
Homogenized steel hot rolled step-by-step reducing thickness to ~11 mm, followed by slow cooling in the oven.

processing_steps.method: water jet cutting (OMAX 2626, Kent, Washington, USA)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples fabricated to accurate geometries with minimized thermal distortion.
Fixed austenitization temperature of 1150 °C applied to S1, S2, S4 and S5 in the dilatometer (Thermal cycle in Fig. 1a: S1, S2, S5: 1150 °C (15 min.)). Heated at 10 K s⁻¹.

processing_steps.method: continuous cooling from austenitization to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹ is sufficiently fast to suppress intermediate phase transformations and ensure fine bainitic transformation.
Austempering at TB = 350 °C; bainitic transformation completed in ~1600 s for S1 (incubation time 100 s), held just above measured Ms = 277 °C to obtain a nano-bainitic microstructure.

processing_steps.method: final cooling after isothermal bainitic hold
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heat-treatment cycle ends with final cooling after the isothermal bainitic hold (Fig. 1a).

structures.overall_structure: Nano-bainitic (nB) microstructure of S1 after austenitizing at 1150 °C; LOM at 1150 °C confirms an αp-free (ferrite-free) matrix. After austempering at 350 °C the structure consists of nano-scale bainitic ferrite laths (nB Type 1 and Type 2) with inter-/intra-sheaf blocky retained austenite and cementite-like (Fe,M)xCy precipitates near γr–bainitic ferrite boundaries.

phases_present.morphology: blocky γr regions between bainitic sheaves (alongside nB types at 350 °C)

defects.lattice_distortion: εα = 0.45 % (bainitic ferrite), εγ = 0.35 % (retained austenite); for S1 at 350 °C εα was notably higher (0.30–0.45 %), indicating clearer heterogeneous dislocation distribution

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: standard deviation of Lt(t) = 23 nm (broader thickness range at 350 °C)

precipitates.type: (Fe,M)xCy carbide (cementite-like, modified by Si and Mo)
precipitates.distribution: located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries; formed primarily during cooling/prior processing (above the bainitic hold temperature); no micro-void formation observed

interfaces.phase_evolution: Austenitizing at 1150 °C dissolves carbides and suppresses polygonal ferrite (αp-free per LOM at 1150 °C); on cooling at 100 K s⁻¹ (Fe,M)xCy nucleates above the bainitic hold temperature; during austempering at 350 °C bainitic ferrite laths (nB Type 1/Type 2) grow with blocky retained austenite forming between sheaves, giving an incomplete-reaction structure with high Vγ (34 %).
interfaces.interface_notes: (Fe,M)xCy precipitates are located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries and are presumed to have negligible influence on tensile properties (no micro-void formation). No explicit interfacial coherency data reported for S1.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens heat-treated in the DIL 805A dilatometer applying the thermal cycle of Fig. 1(a); universal testing machine Zwick/Roell (250 kN load cell). Room temperature not explicitly stated.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Product of strength and elongation (PSE): S1 ~12,000 MPa·% vs S4 ~13,600 MPa·% at TA 1150 °C (S4 at TB 320 °C)

characterization_methods.technique: dilatometry (RLC vs time and RLC vs temperature) and Ms tangent-intersection analysis
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA); cylindrical specimens (∅5 x 10 mm³)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: heating 10 K s⁻¹, austenitizing 1150 °C/15 min, cooling 100 K s⁻¹
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine TA, Ms and the bainitic transformation finish time (Bt) from the onset of the RLC plateau
characterization_methods.key_findings: For S1 Ms = 277 °C; at TB 350 °C bainitic transformation completed in ~1600 s with an incubation time of 100 s.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG (Jena, Germany); 6 % Nital etching
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LOM at 1050 °C benchmark and at selected TA 1150 °C for S1
characterization_methods.purpose: Verify elimination of polygonal ferrite (αp) after austenitization
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1 shows αp at 1050 °C but is αp-free at 1150 °C (Fig. 3a).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer, Cu Kα (40 kV/40 mA), PIXcel 1D detector
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine retained-austenite volume fraction (Vγ) and phase micro-strains (εγ, εα)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For S1 (Fig. 2a example) Vγ = 34 % with εγ = 0.35 % and εα = 0.45 % at TB 350 °C.

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG SEM and Oxford Instruments EDX; gold sputter-coated etched samples
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM of S1 at TB 300 °C and 350 °C; bainite thickness measured by ImageJ (100 measurements from 10 images)
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze bainitic lamellar thickness and precipitate (Fe,M)xCy morphology/composition
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1 at 350 °C shows nB Type 1/Type 2 with blocky γr and rounded (Fe,M)xCy particles near γr–bainitic ferrite boundaries; no κ-carbide plates observed; EDX indicates Si and Mo within the carbides.

computational_details.simulation_method: MatCalc thermodynamic equilibrium and precipitation-kinetics (TTP) calculations
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc (Version 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Phases considered: fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC system; Ti-Mo-C and (Fe,M)xCy carbide systems kinetically simulated via a precipitation-kinetics model based on heterogeneous nucleation theory (dislocation and grain-boundary nucleation sites, ortho-equilibrium transformation) with volumetric misfit considered; κ-carbides treated as fixed phase fractions.
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Applied austenitization TA 1150 °C; cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹; austempering at TB 350 °C (and 300 °C) for the bainitic transformation.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: MatCalc ferrite-free TA (991 °C) and carbide-dissolution Tcd (1103 °C) for S1 were compared against dilatometric/measured TA (1062 °C) and LOM; (1−Vc)=0.78 used with XRD. Simulated precipitation of (Fe,M)xCy above the bainitic hold temperature agreed with SEM observations.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute Vγ from integrated α/γ XRD peak intensities and carbide fraction (1−Vc)
analytical_models.model_note: Vγ = (1−Vc)(Iγ/Rγ)/[(Iα/Rα)+(Iγ/Rγ)], where Iγ, Iα are integrated intensities and Rγ, Rα the theoretical relative intensities.

unmapped_findings: S1 (TA 1150 °C) measured martensite-start temperature Ms = 277 °C (Table 2 / Fig. 4 / Fig. 5a).
MatCalc-predicted ferrite-free austenitizing temperature for S1 = 991 °C; measured TA = 1062 °C; applied TA = 1150 °C; carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd = 1103 °C (Table 2, Fig. 4a).
S1 at 1150 °C was αp-free (polygonal ferrite eliminated) as confirmed by LOM (Fig. 3a).
Bainitic transformation finish time Bt for S1 at TB 350 °C ≈ 1600 s with an incubation time of 100 s (Section 3.2; Fig. 1b, Fig. 6c).
Product of strength and elongation (PSE) for S1 at TB 350 °C ≈ 12,000 MPa·% (Section 3.3).
S1 at TB 300 °C reached the maximum Rp0.2 of 1225 MPa among all samples; this value corresponds to the S1 TA1150/TB300 condition (sibling), not to the TB 350 °C sample.

Fig. 7 hardness series (left to right: 464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493 HV30) is assigned first to S1 TA1150/TB350; this ordering is inferred from the categorical axis and the statement that HV30 is higher at lower TB (except S4).
For S1, Vγ rose to 34 % at the higher TB (350 °C) versus 27 % at the lower TB (300 °C), showing a more pronounced incomplete-reaction character at 350 °C.
S1 and S2 exhibit only minor differences (~0.1 wt.% C variation) with negligible effect on the overall mechanical response.

MatCalc TTP (Fig. 8a) indicates (Fe,M)xCy precipitates unavoidably during cooling between approximately 700 °C and 1150 °C for S1; these precipitates formed above the bainitic hold temperature and had negligible influence on tensile properties.
